messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm seeing a recurring jitter pattern for small-tenant requests in the continuous batcher. p95 looks fine but p999 spikes when micro-requests land interleaved with big streams. Thinking about a lightweight tail-hedging + smoothing window to reduce jitter without blowing up cost. anyone tried this in prod?

liam: We experimented with hedging for <50-token reqs last quarter. It dropped tails but doubled token count when the hedges fired. cost was the killer.

sarah: Are the spikes correlated with KV cache misses or queue reshuffles? Hedging duplicates can increase KV pressure and hurt downstream latency.

maya: Mixed. Some spikes line up with KV cold misses, some when a high-throughput tenant temporarily monopolizes a slab and starves micro windows.

devon: Could we do probabilistic hedging? e.g., only hedge when queue-latency > threshold and tenant doesn’t have lease headroom. That reduces duplicate rate.

liam: Probabilistic helps but adds complexity to admission. We saw oscillation where hedged responses cause earlier admits that cancel later ones — need idempotency/duplicate-filtering.

sarah: Another axis: smoothing window shape. Instead of fixed micro-window, use an EWMA of arrival intervals per-tenant to adapt window length. Smarter than static thresholds.

maya: EWMA idea sounds good. downside: slower responsiveness for sudden burts? might increase latency for legitimate bursts.

devon: We can combine: EWMA-based base window + fast-path drain if tenant is above a throughput ratio. Also consider token-based shaping: cap batch token budget per tenant per-window.

liam: Token-budgeting is nice because it ties directly to cost. But requires accurate token estimation up-front; tricky for chat-style messages.

sarah: For KV concern: add a lightweight cache-score check to decide to hedge. if cached-prefix-score > X, prefer hedging; else avoid. cheap approximation: prefix-hit=true/false.

maya: Sketch of a possible rule set: 1) if request.tokens < 64 and queue_latency > 6ms and tenant_headroom == 0 -> probabilistic hedge(10%). 2) EWMA window multiplier per-tenant with min=1ms max=10ms. 3) per-window token budget enforcement. 4) record hedged_dups metric and apply kill-switch if >5% of origin traffic.

liam: That addresses cost and KV. Need to think about telemetry: hedged_dup_latency, hedged_dup_cost, kv_miss_rate_post_hedge.

devon: Also ensure canonical de-dup key: (tenant, request_id, seq_hash). If duplicate arrives later, drop gracefully. implement in batcher at enqueue stage.

sarah: Another tradeoff: hedging hides bad scheduling decisions. If we rely on hedges, we may never fix slab starving problems. Should pair with an eviction/reshuffle alert.

maya: Agreed. Add alert: slab_starvation_p95>threshold triggers tenant rebalancing playbook.

liam: Ops question — how to test without real traffic? feature-flagged rollout with traffic mirroring and canary percent. Use synthetic micro-requests that mimic small-tenants to exercise hedging path.

maya: Proposed rollout plan: feature flag -> 1% tenants for 24h -> metrics review (cost + p999) -> 5% -> runbook check -> 25% -> escalate.

devon: Small config example for runtime (proto-ish):
```
hedging {
  enabled: true
  base_probability: 0.0
  conditional_probability: 0.1 // when latency & headroom rules hit
  max_dup_rate_kill_switch: 0.05
}
window {
  ewma_alpha: 0.2
  min_ms: 1
  max_ms: 10
}
token_budget_per_window: 1024
```

sarah: One more edge: streaming responses. If a hedged fast-path returns a partial stream then a slower full stream arrives, need to reconcile. Our batcher should prefer whichever completes first and cancel others; ensure downstream tool-calls are deduplicated.

maya: Good point. We'll need a cancel token handshake to avoid executing duplicate tool-calls. add to implementation notes.

liam: TL;DR tradeoffs: hedging reduces tail but increases cost and KV pressure; EWMA smoothing adapts to tenant patterns but can lag bursts; token budgets constrain cost but need good estimates; de-dupe and cancel tokens required for correctness.

maya: Action items: (1) devon + liam to prototype probabilistic hedger + ewma window in dev cluster (2w). (2) sarah to add KV-score fast-path check & metrics. (3) ops to draft rollout + kill-switch playbook. I'll open RFC follow-up with config knobs and canary plan.

scheduler-bot: New RFC follow-up created: rfc/continuous-batcher/1768123456-tail-hedging-draft — assign owners devon, liam, sarah, maya

devon: I'll start a small PoC branch and drop perf numbers once we have baseline.

liam: I'll add the de-dupe key sketch and cancel handshake in the batcher API doc.

sarah: I'll add the hedged metrics to the telemetry board and a dashboard for quick check.

maya: Thanks all. keep it tight on kill-switch thresholds — we don't want cost surprises. :eyes:

liam: ack

sarah: ack

devon: ack
